newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen steady for now, more gains expected.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen steady for now, more gains expected.

text.p: Germany's 30-share DAX index was expected to take a breather in Monday trading after Friday's rise to dizzy record heights, but dealers said the uptrend remained intact and further gains were likely soon.
The 30-share IBIS DAX, which on Friday stormed up to a record level, was trading down 3.03 points at 3,943.70, around 20 points below the new all-time high of 3,965.61.

Dealers said a moderate ease in the dollar to around 1.7440 marks at 0755 GMT was a negative for the market. "We are having to battle against a slightly lower dollar," one trader at a German bank said. "It is braking us somewhat."
"As there are no notable figures due today, we expect a rather quiet day," DTB DAX traders at SuedwestLB commented.
At the same time, traders were clearly optimistic for the market in the medium term.
"The risk in the German share market at the moment is not to be invested in it," Susanne Schneemayer at Hypo-Research said in a morning commentary.

"The status of our multi factor model improved to show four rather than three positive indicators in the course of June," she said. "Such a status has in the past signaled a performance of 15-20 percent in the DAX over the upcoming 12 months."

A focal point in today's market was Pro Sieben, with shares listing in Frankfurt today. The issue, which was 50 times oversubscribed, was made at the top end of the the subscription range of 72 marks.
Pro Sieben shares were trading at 106.00 to 110.00 marks in the grey market, according to share market dealers, after earlier trading as high as 112 marks in morning dealings.
But the shares were below the 120 marks seen last week.
"The dealings are very active," said one trader. "I think the bids will remain relatively strong."
